title: 1995 AHSME Problem 15
statement: Five points on a circle are numbered \(1,\) \(2,\) \(3,\) \(4,\) and \(5\) in clockwise order. A bug jumps in a clockwise direction from one point to another around the circle; if it is on an odd-numbered point, it moves one point, and if it is on an even-numbered point, it moves two points. If the bug begins on point \(5,\) after \(1995\) jumps it will be on point

solutions.text: Starting at \(5,\) the landing points are \(1,2,4,1,2,4,\ldots\) Thus the cycle \(1,2,4\) has length \(3.\) Since \(1995\) is divisible by \(3,\) the \(1995\)th landing point is \(4.\) Thus the correct answer is D.
hints: Write down the landing points for the first few jumps
Once a point repeats, reduce the remaining number of jumps modulo the cycle length
